[gameplay]

Its a 2d pixelated turn-based rogulike rpg game, while characters and environment are pixelated, lighting effects and shadows that result from explosion lighting are 3d, added with the game's high frame rate gives it a unique artistic look

The main idea is that you fight against a group of cyborgs who try to take over every dimension of the galaxy, that being said, it seems like you only have one world to venture into but in different realities that change everytime you die and try again in another run, the game takes inspiration from known games that will be mentioned below

You start with three characters, but you can collect a certain item that can be used in your base to buy new tech, upgrades and unlock more characters

You leave your base and visit a different reality of the same planet that changes its layout everytime you revisit, you start exploring the map in top down view, there are different section with points connecting them, and since its a rogulike game where the map layout changes, that means that the placement of enemy troops, treasure chests and tech items changes as well

Whenever you transition from one sector to another, you consume certain points, when those points reach zero, night falls and you must camp to recharge those points, the camping system is heavily inspired by the Darkest Dungeon where you use special ability cards that either restore health or bestow shield or other special effects, and each character has its own camping cards, and just like darkest dungeon, each camping ability can only be used once in the same night and it costs camping points as well, once you run out of either cards or camping points, you go to sleep, using cards on allies instead on self will increase friendship between those two characters

You only have three days to explore the map, and it's kinda hard to explore all of it, so choose your path wisely, after three days, you will be forced to fight against the boss "known as behemoth" who lands on the planet to take it over, you can off course choose to fight the behemoth early before the time runs out, you just have to reach an objective marked on the map but it's recommended that you collect weapons and upgrades before that

The fighting system is a bit complicated and full of numbers, but I'll try to focus on the most important elements, first and foremost, you can see who the enemy is going to attack in every turn and what attack it'll use and what damage and special effects the attack has just like Slay the Spire, each unit involved in combat has both health and shield, your characters shields regenerate after combat but health can only be restored through items, healing stations or camping abilities

The two most important factors you need to watch out for are the time meter and the crit bonus effects, the time meter is displayed in the top of the screen and it shows when each unit will have its turn to attack, the crit bonus effects can only activate if you managed to hit an enemy unit before it manages to attack, keep in mind the reverse is also true

Based on those two factors, there is a trick that is so useful and crucial, and that is coordinating your attacks in a way that'll result in breaking the enemy unit which means preventing it from attacking this turn, how to do that? Well, each attack your units can do has a delay/push back effect (you can see it in your attacks parameters, it's colored in green) and it activates along with the crit bonus which means as mentioned above that it'll only activate if you attack the enemy unit before it attacks, different attacks have different delaying power, whenever you select an attack and highlight an enemy unit, pay attention to the character icon in the time meter in the upper middle section of the screen, it'll show you how much delay your attack will cause to that enemy unit, if your combined attacks pushed the enemy icon to the far end of the meter, then the breaking effect happens and that unit loses its right to attack this turn, pretty useful when dealing with enemies who are preparing to use powerful attacks on your members, just keep an eye on the yellow numbers right next to the enemy unit icon in the time meter, these numbers show how many attacks can push the enemy back, if they reach zero then that unit gains immunity to push back effect until the end of that turn, so don't waste the number of delays you can cause on attacks with weak push back power unless you had to

There are combination attacks that your units can execute together if the relationship between them is strong enough, as mentioned above, friendship can increase during camping when a character uses its camping restoration or bonus effects on another character

While there is no gore when attacking, still from what I noticed, your units (the fleshy ones) has a bit gruesome death animations, the enemy units are mostly cyborgs and bots so nothing gory about their death animations, unless there are more enemies who are human, animalistic or plant-like, personally I haven't seen any aside mechanical enemies

Speaking of enemies, not all of them are random 100‪% percent, the game takes heavy inspiration from shadow of mordor, there are enemy commanders and officials with a chain of command, and there is a menu you can view where it shows you who they are, what are their names, strengths and weaknesses, those of them who kill you may get promotions, and those you kill may get replaced after sometime, and you don't know when you'll encounter one of them during your adventures

You can level up your characters mid adventure, increasing their stats and unlocking new attacks or abilities, however when you die and go for another run, your characters go back to level 1 and the equipment they found in their previous adventures are gone, there are some upgrades you can buy in your base, i haven't checked them all but I'm sure some if them may help your characters maintain some of the progress they made in their previous
